To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the correctness of an execution at isolation levels lower that SERIALIZABLE depends on the application's semantic requirements; and (b) the execution of a transaction at a lower level will be semantically correct if it is serializable at that level and if all transactions that access the same data are executing at the same isolation level.

the execution of an ACID application at an ANSI/ISO isolation level other than SERIALIZAL is correct if and only if the following conditions hold: (1) The application is correct at the SERIALIZABLE isolation level, and (2) the application does not contain any of the following anomalies: a non-repeatable read, a dirty read, or a write skew.

(1) for any isolation level, there is a condition under which transactions executing at that level will produce a correct result, (2) this condition is a necessary and sufficient condition for the execution of transactions to be semantically correct, and (3) the condition is a function of the application and is not dependent on the database schema.
